content:
# Judith Chapter 7 — Disagreement Log
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Summary
**Total Disagreements: 24**
Chapter 7 is a military and humanitarian chapter — the siege logistics, the dry wells, and the near-collapse of Bethulia. Disagreements fall into three clusters: military/geographic terminology, vivid description of suffering, and the people's desperate speech to Uzziah.

---

## Disagreements

**1. v. 2 — Army count introduction**
- EMET: "the force of their armies was a hundred and seventy thousand"
- LOGOS: "their combined forces numbered one hundred and seventy thousand"
- PNEUMA: "their combined might came to one hundred and seventy thousand"
- SOPHIA ruling: "their combined forces numbered" (LOGOS)

**2. v. 3 — "they-spread out in breadth" / "spreading out as far as"**
- EMET: "they-spread out in breadth over Dothaim as-far-as Belmaim"
- LOGOS: "spreading out as far as Dothaim in breadth"
- PNEUMA: "Their lines stretched from Dothaim in the west to Belmaim"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — most faithful to Greek structure; PNEUMA adds "west" which is not in the text

**3. v. 4 — "lick-clean the face of the land" idiom**
- EMET: "these will lick-clean the face of all the land"
- LOGOS: "these men will devour the whole face of the land"
- PNEUMA: "these men will strip the land bare"
- SOPHIA ruling: "devour the whole face of the land" — preserves "face of the land" while moderating the idiom

**4. v. 4 — "bear the weight of their force"**
- EMET: "will not bear the weight of their force"
- LOGOS: "can sustain the weight of their forces"
- PNEUMA: "can contain an army this size"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "sustain" is precise; PNEUMA loses the weight metaphor

**5. v. 6 — "on the second day" — cavalry display**
- EMET: "Holofernes led-out all his-cavalry before the sons of Israel"
- LOGOS: "Holofernes led out all his cavalry before the Israelites"
- PNEUMA: "Holofernes rode out with his full cavalry force to reconnoiter"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — PNEUMA combines vv. 6-7 into one action, losing the deliberate two-step

**6. v. 7 — "he surveyed / reconnoitered"**
- EMET: "he surveyed the ascents of their city"
- LOGOS: "reconnoitered the approaches to their city"
- PNEUMA: (merged with v. 6)
- SOPHIA ruling: "reconnoitered the approaches" (LOGOS — military precision)

**7. v. 8 — "sons of Esau" vs. "Edomites"**
- EMET: "all the chiefs of the sons of Esau"
- LOGOS: "all the chieftains of the Edomites"
- PNEUMA: "chiefs of the Edomites"
- SOPHIA ruling: "chieftains of the Edomites" — standard biblical identification; EMET's "sons of Esau" is technically more literal but less conventional

**8. v. 10 — "they do not trust in their spears"**
- EMET: "do not trust in their spears"
- LOGOS: "do not rely on their spears"
- PNEUMA: "do not fight with spears"
- SOPHIA ruling: "do not rely on their spears" (LOGOS — *pepoithasin* = trust/rely on)

**9. v. 12 — "hold-in-possession" / "hold" / "take control of"**
- EMET: "let your-servants hold-in-possession the spring"
- LOGOS: "have your servants hold the spring"
- PNEUMA: "send your men to take control of the spring"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "hold" is adequate; EMET's compound is awkward in English

**10. v. 13 — "thirst will destroy them"**
- EMET: "thirst will-destroy them"
- LOGOS: "thirst will destroy them"
- PNEUMA: "thirst will do your fighting for you"
- SOPHIA ruling: "thirst will destroy them" — PNEUMA paraphrase loses the passive-divine-instrument sense

**11. v. 14 — "they-will-be-laid-low in-the streets"**
- EMET: "they-will-be-laid-low in the streets where they dwell"
- LOGOS: "they will be laid out in the streets where they live"
- PNEUMA: "dying in the streets before a sword even touches them"
- SOPHIA ruling: "laid out dead in the streets where they live" (blends EMET/LOGOS)

**12. v. 15 — "repay them with evil"**
- EMET: "you will repay them with evil"
- LOGOS: "you will exact bitter payment from them"
- PNEUMA: "they will pay for their defiance"
- SOPHIA ruling: EMET/LOGOS blend: "you will repay them with evil" — most literal to *apodōseis autois kaka*

**13. v. 18 — "covered all the face of the land"**
- EMET: "covered all the face of the land"
- LOGOS: "covering the entire face of the land"
- PNEUMA: "spread across the plain like a flood"
- SOPHIA ruling: "covered the entire face of the land" (LOGOS) — PNEUMA's simile is not in the text

**14. v. 19 — "their spirit sank" / "their spirits sank"**
- EMET: "their spirit-sank" (singular *psyche*)
- LOGOS: "their spirits sank"
- PNEUMA: "their spirits collapsed"
- SOPHIA ruling: "their spirits sank" — natural English plural acceptable

**15. v. 20 — duration: "thirty-four days"**
- All three agree: thirty-four days
- No disagreement

**16. v. 21 — "measured out as a ration"**
- EMET: "measured out as a ration for drinking"
- LOGOS: "rationed out by measure"
- PNEUMA: "doled out by ration"
- SOPHIA ruling: "rationed out by measure" (LOGOS — captures both the measuring and the rationing)

**17. v. 22 — "dispirited" vs. "limp"**
- EMET: "children were-dispirited" (*oligopsychei* = faint of soul)
- LOGOS: "children were dispirited"
- PNEUMA: "children went limp"
- SOPHIA ruling: "dispirited" — preserves the soul-language of the Greek

**18. v. 22 — "passages of the gates"**
- EMET: "in the passages of-the gates"
- LOGOS: "in the gateways"
- PNEUMA: "at the city gates"
- SOPHIA ruling: "at the passages of the gates" — the Greek *en tais diodois* means passageways/thoroughfares

**19. v. 24 — "you have done us great harm" / "you have ruined us"**
- EMET: "you have done us great harm in not seeking peace"
- LOGOS: "you have done us great wrong in refusing to make peace"
- PNEUMA: "you have ruined us by refusing to make peace"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "great wrong" preserves *megas*; "ruined" is too interpretive

**20. v. 25 — "God has sold us into their hands"**
- EMET: "God has-sold us into their hands"
- LOGOS: "God has sold us into their hands"
- PNEUMA: "God has handed us over to them"
- SOPHIA ruling: "God has sold us into their hands" — *apedoto* = sold; preserves the stinging theology

**21. v. 27 — "plunder" — vocabulary consistency**
- EMET: "become plunder for them"
- LOGOS: "become their plunder"
- PNEUMA: "being plunder is better than being dead"
- SOPHIA ruling: "become their plunder" (LOGOS)

**22. v. 28 — "call to witness" formula**
- EMET: "We-call-to-witness against you heaven and earth and our God"
- LOGOS: "We call heaven and earth and our God to witness against you"
- PNEUMA: "We call heaven and earth and our God — the Lord of our ancestors — to witness against you"
- SOPHIA ruling: "We call to witness against you heaven and earth and our God and the Lord of our ancestors" (EMET order, expanded)

**23. v. 30 — "turn his mercy" / "show us mercy" / "relent"**
- EMET: "the Lord our God will turn his mercy upon us"
- LOGOS: "the Lord our God may yet turn his compassion toward us"
- PNEUMA: "the Lord our God may still relent"
- SOPHIA ruling: "the Lord our God may turn his mercy toward us" — *eleēsēi* = show mercy; PNEUMA's "relent" is paraphrase

**24. v. 32 — "brought very low in distress"**
- EMET: "they were brought-very-low in the city"
- LOGOS: "they were in great distress throughout the city"
- PNEUMA: "misery settled over every corner of the city"
- SOPHIA ruling: "the city was brought very low in distress" (blends both — preserves the Greek *katepseugmenoi* = cast down/brought low)
